One-shot export of a corpus to Zotero

Source: R/corpus_to_zotero.R
corpus_to_zotero.Rd

Convenience wrapper: maps a corpus to CSL JSON with corpus_to_csljson() (in a temporary directory, removed afterwards) and imports it into the library selected in Zotero with csljson_to_zotero(). See there for re-exports (existing), tags, collections and the import speed.

Usage

corpus_to_zotero(
  project_dir,
  corpus = file.path(project_dir, "parquet"),
  existing = c("skip", "update", "overwrite"),
  tags,
  collection,
  chunk_size = 1000,
  ...
)

Arguments

project_dir

Optional path to the project directory, used for the default of corpus.

corpus

Path to parquet dataset, Arrow Dataset/Table or data.frame/tibble of works. Default file.path(project_dir, "parquet").

existing

"skip" (default), "update" or "overwrite": what to do with works already in the Zotero library. See csljson_to_zotero().

tags

Tags to write, by OpenAlex ID (see "Tags" in csljson_to_zotero()): a data.frame, a parquet path, or NULL for none. Default: <project_dir>/zotero_tags.parquet (written by zotero_tags()) if it exists, else NULL.

collection

Path of the Zotero collection to export into. Default: c(<name of project_dir>, <name of corpus>), leaving out what has no name (a corpus given as a data.frame); .parquet is dropped from the corpus name. NULL puts the works only into what is selected in Zotero.

chunk_size

Works per file sent to Zotero. Default 1000, which gives progress per 1000 works and stays well within timeout.

...

Further arguments to csljson_to_zotero() (method, url, api_key, timeout).

Value

Invisibly, the data.frame returned by csljson_to_zotero(), one row per chunk.

Details

By default the works go into their own nested collection, named after the project directory and the corpus (<project> > <corpus>), so an accidental export is easy to find and delete. Select the library itself in Zotero (not a collection) before exporting.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# In Zotero, select the target library or collection first.
res <- corpus_to_zotero("my_project")
subset(res, !ok)
} # }
